column1: # Query actions that a handler dispatches but routing does not send to that handler.
# Columns: service, action, service it reaches instead.
# Routing only matters when a request arrives without a usable credential scope, since
# otherwise the service comes from the SigV4 scope. On that path there is the action name
# and the Version the request declares, and AwsQueryServiceResolver backs
# IamEnforcementFilter too, so an entry here is also authorized under the wrong namespace.
# Every entry is a name missing from its own service's routing set, and adding it there
# is the fix, as #5032 did for IAM. The third column only says where the request goes
# meanwhile: sqs when no set holds the name, since that is the default, or the service
# whose set does. A name two services define needs nothing more than being in both sets,
# because the Version a request carries decides between them.
# A request without a Version, which only a hand-rolled client sends, is the one other
# way to land here. A name two services define then goes to the one tried first, which
# is a gap when that one does not handle the name.
# 170 entries: 170 unrouted, 0 claimed by another service.
# Shrink this file, never grow it. Removing a line is the point; adding one needs a
# reason in the PR that adds it. AwsQueryActionRoutingParityTest fails on an entry that
# is no longer a gap, so a fix cannot leave the list stale.
